skill.name: form-testing
skill.description: Test WordPress contact forms, SMTP settings, and email delivery with WP-CLI, curl, and Docker-based checks.
skill.summary: Validate WordPress forms, SMTP configuration, and email delivery from containerized sites.
skill.author: CrazySwami

security_audit.summary: Most SKILL.md backtick and URL findings are documentation false positives, and no prompt injection was found. The skill still has real shell, WP-CLI, SMTP inspection, and outbound email capabilities. High-risk issues remain in scripts/test-mail.sh because the recipient is unescaped in wp eval and defaults to an external email address.

remediation.issue: Recipient argument is interpolated into wp eval PHP code.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the recipient with a strict email parser and pass it through safe encoding before wp eval. Prefer a temporary file or WP-CLI option that avoids code interpolation.

remediation.issue: The test script defaults to an external recipient address.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the external default and require an explicit approved recipient. A local site administrator address is safer than a vendor-controlled address.

remediation.issue: SMTP configuration commands can expose credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Do not show real passwords in prompts or command history. Use environment variables, secret managers, or interactive input with redacted output.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting commands can reveal mail logs and SMTP metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Add warnings to run only on authorized systems and redact recipient, host, and log details before sharing audit reports.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped Recipient In WP-CLI Eval
semantic_findings.description: scripts/test-mail.sh inserts the recipient argument directly into PHP code passed to wp eval. A crafted value containing a quote can break out of the string and run PHP inside the WordPress container.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script assigns TO_EMAIL from user input and interpolates it into a quoted PHP string inside wp eval without escaping. This is a direct code injection pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Hard-Coded External Test Recipient
semantic_findings.description: The test email recipient defaults to admin@csrdevelopment.com. If the script runs without an explicit recipient, it sends site URL, PHP version, and WordPress version to that external address.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The default recipient is hard-coded, and the message body clearly includes site and version details before calling wp_mail. This is strong evidence of unintended outbound disclosure.

semantic_findings.title: SMTP Credentials In Command-Line Example
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md shows SMTP username and password fields inside a wp option update command. Users who paste real values can expose secrets through shell history, process listings, or shared logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The credentials are placeholders, not leaked real secrets. The risk is still credible because the documented command pattern encourages placing live secrets on the command line.

content.user_title: Test WordPress Forms and Email Delivery
content.value_statement: WordPress teams need proof that forms submit correctly and messages reach inboxes. This skill provides WP-CLI and curl checks for email delivery, SMTP settings, and form behavior.
actual_capabilities: Sends WP-CLI wp_mail test messages to a configured recipient.
Checks whether the WP Mail SMTP plugin is active.
Reads SMTP host, port, encryption, and auth status.
Provides curl examples for contact form submission tests.
Documents nonce, sanitization, redirect, and email receipt checks.
Includes troubleshooting steps for WordPress email failures.
limitations: Requires shell, Docker, and WP-CLI access to the target WordPress container.
Can send real email and should only run on authorized sites.
Does not crawl every form automatically.
Some examples are tailored to CSR theme form names.

use_cases.title: Verify Site Email Delivery
use_cases.description: Check SMTP plugin status and send a controlled test message after a migration or launch.

use_cases.title: Test Contact Form Behavior
use_cases.description: Submit a known form payload and confirm redirects, validation, and admin email receipt.

use_cases.title: Audit Form Security Basics
use_cases.description: Review nonce usage, input sanitization, reply-to handling, and email header safety.

prompt_templates.title: Check Email Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for one WordPress container.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the WP Mail SMTP status for my WordPress container named [container]. Do not send email yet.

prompt_templates.title: Send Test Message
prompt_templates.scenario: Controlled delivery test with an approved recipient.
prompt_templates.prompt: Send one WordPress test email from [container] to [approved address]. Summarize the result and any mailer error.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Contact Form
prompt_templates.scenario: Form submission test for a known page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Test the contact form at [authorized URL] with safe sample data. Report validation, redirects, and delivery checks.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Form Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit forms on [authorized site]. Check SMTP, test delivery, verify nonce behavior, and produce prioritized remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Check email delivery in the wordpress container for ops@example.com.
output_examples.output: Result: SMTP plugin active. Test message sent to the approved recipient. No PHPMailer error was reported.

output_examples.input: Review the contact page form before launch.
output_examples.output: Report: required fields validated, redirect confirmed, admin email received, and nonce protection should be reviewed.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot missing form emails after migration.
output_examples.output: Findings: SMTP settings are incomplete. Configure an approved mailer, send a new test message, and verify DNS records.

best_practices: Run tests only on sites and containers you are authorized to access.
Use an explicit approved recipient for every email test.
Redact SMTP details before sharing reports or tickets.
anti_patterns: Do not test forms on third-party sites without permission.
Do not rely on default recipient addresses for delivery tests.
Do not paste real SMTP passwords into prompts or public issue trackers.

faq.question: Does this skill send real email?
faq.answer: Yes. The test script can send a real WordPress email to the chosen recipient.

faq.question: What access is required?
faq.answer: You need shell access, Docker access, and WP-CLI access to the WordPress container.

faq.question: Can it test any contact form plugin?
faq.answer: It gives general curl and audit steps, but some examples use CSR theme field names.

faq.question: Does it verify inbox receipt automatically?
faq.answer: No. It sends test messages and reports WordPress errors. A human still checks the inbox.

faq.question: Is it safe for production?
faq.answer: Use it carefully with approved recipients. Prefer staging when testing form behavior.

faq.question: Does it store SMTP credentials?
faq.answer: The examples show WordPress SMTP configuration. Real credentials should be handled outside prompts and logs.
